description: We are students from different corners of India, we are interested in how real world problems can be solved by AI/ML. We are here eager to collaborate and build something meaningful through the NASA Space Apps Challenge.
summary:
AXON LunarSight is a project that aims to make exploring the Moon easier and more interactive, much like Google Maps does for Earth. It is designed to help users explore different lunar locations and learn about NASA's Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) missions.
Users can explore lunar landing sites and examine important conditions such as sunlight availability, Sun elevation and Earth's visibility from a selected location and time. The project also aims to help users compare different landing sites and understand the opportunities and challenges each location may offer.
Our goal is to bring useful lunar mission information together in one place and make it easier for students, researchers and space enthusiasts to understand the Moon and the factors involved in planning future lunar missions.
details:
We are building AXON LunarSight to make lunar exploration information easier to access and understand. The idea is to create an interactive map of the Moon where users can explore different locations and learn about NASA's CLPS missions.

The application is designed to let users select a lunar location and a date and time to study conditions such as the Sun's elevation, sunlight availability and whether Earth is geometrically visible from that location. We also aim to provide timelines and comparison features to help users examine different landing sites.

We are developing the project using modern web technologies, including React and TypeScript for the frontend and Python with FastAPI for the backend. Our scientific computing work uses space-science tools and relevant lunar data to support the calculations.

What makes this project interesting is that it brings several important aspects of lunar mission planning into one interactive platform. Instead of searching through different sources, users can explore the information in a more visual and understandable way.

Our aim is to make lunar exploration more accessible while helping users understand some of the real scientific factors that matter when selecting potential lunar landing locations.
